name: Paraguay
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting on Paraguay: agribusiness and land due diligence, beneficial ownership research, tri-border trade risk and asset inquiries.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Paraguay often concerns agribusiness and land counterparties, ownership behind trading companies in the tri-border region, and assets held through Paraguayan entities. TDSC scopes the work from Nashville and coordinates qualified Paraguayan professionals and counsel where local inquiries are needed.
intro: Paraguay is a civil law jurisdiction with a unified Civil Code covering civil and commercial obligations, a bilingual Spanish and Guarani society, and an economy built on soybeans, beef, hydroelectric power and re-export trade. Its transparency framework has expanded in recent years. Ley 6446 of 2019 created administrative registers of legal persons and structures and of beneficial owners, kept through the Abogacía del Tesoro, and a comprehensive personal data protection law, Ley 7593/2025, was promulgated in November 2025, with obligations phasing in towards late 2027. Records are improving but uneven, and much ownership information still has to be assembled from several sources.

Organisations commission work involving Paraguay for several reasons. International grain traders, meatpackers and investors in the Chaco and eastern farmland need to verify counterparties, land title and environmental compliance. Brands and distributors face counterfeit and contraband risk linked to Ciudad del Este and the border with Brazil and Argentina. Manufacturers using Paraguay's maquila regime to supply Brazil need partner checks. Lenders and litigants pursue assets after defaults, and compliance teams screen counterparties for money laundering exposure in a jurisdiction that GAFILAT evaluations have pushed to tighten beneficial ownership and anti-corruption rules.

population.value: approximately 6.1 million (2022 national census, as reported)

legal_system: Paraguay has a civil law system based on the 1992 Constitution and codified law, including a Civil Code that unifies civil and commercial obligations. Commercial disputes are heard by first-instance civil and commercial courts, with appeals to the Tribunales de Apelación en lo Civil y Comercial and final review by the Corte Suprema de Justicia, whose Constitutional Chamber hears constitutionality actions. There is no separate commercial court system. Arbitration is available under the national arbitration and mediation law, with an institutional centre attached to the national chamber of commerce in Asunción. Proceedings are in Spanish.

data_protection.law: Ley N.° 7593/2025 de Protección de Datos Personales en la República del Paraguay (promulgated 28 November 2025)
data_protection.regulator: Agencia Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales, under the Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies (MITIC)
data_protection.summary: Ley 7593/2025 is Paraguay's first comprehensive personal data protection law and applies to both public and private sectors. It gives individuals rights to know what data is held and why, to correction, deletion and objection, and adds protection for sensitive data, including biometric, genetic, political, religious and sexual-orientation data, and for minors. The government has indicated it will take effect progressively from late 2027, with regulations still to set concrete deadlines. Until then, privacy rests on constitutional protections and earlier sectoral rules. For investigative work, organisations should already document purpose and proportionality, limit sensitive data, and treat transfers of Paraguayan personal data abroad cautiously pending regulations.

investigator_regulation: We have not identified a dedicated licensing regime for private investigators in Paraguay in the sources reviewed for this page, and the position should be confirmed with Paraguayan counsel for each engagement. Interception of communications and access to criminal, tax, migration and banking records are reserved to authorities acting under legal process, and constitutional privacy protections apply to covert recording and intrusive observation. In practice, inquiries in Paraguay rely on public registries, court files accessible to parties, and interviews conducted lawfully. TDSC coordinates qualified local professionals and counsel for any field work and does not itself conduct investigations on the ground in Paraguay.
corporate_records: Companies are registered in the public registries administered under the judiciary, with simplified joint-stock companies (EAS) registered through a separate digital procedure. Registry filings record constitution, statutes, directors and powers, and certified copies can be requested. Under Ley 6446/2019 and Decreto 3241/2020, companies, associations, foundations and other legal persons must also register basic data, members, directors and each beneficial owner with the administrative registers kept through the Abogacía del Tesoro, update changes within 15 business days and confirm annually by 30 June. These registers are for authorities and obliged entities rather than open public search. Property records are kept by the real estate registry and national cadastre.
anti_corruption: Paraguay's core anti-money laundering statute is Ley 1015/1997, with the Secretaría de Prevención de Lavado de Dinero o Bienes (SEPRELAD) acting as financial intelligence unit and supervisor; obliged entities must require proof of beneficial ownership registration under Ley 6446/2019. Integrity rules include Ley 7089/2023 on conflicts of interest in public office, amended by Ley 7236/2024, and a package of anti-corruption laws promulgated ahead of a GAFILAT evaluation. Prosecution rests with the Ministerio Público, and the Contraloría General de la República audits public spending.

matters.title: Farmland and agribusiness diligence
matters.text: Verifying owners, title chains and encumbrances for farmland and ranches in the eastern departments and the Chaco, along with environmental and deforestation compliance, before grain traders, meatpackers and investors commit capital or enter supply agreements.

matters.title: Tri-border trade counterparties
matters.text: Background and ownership research on importers, distributors and trading houses in Ciudad del Este and border towns, where re-export, contraband and counterfeit risks require brands and suppliers to confirm who they are actually dealing with.

matters.title: Maquila and industrial partner checks
matters.text: Reviewing ownership, litigation and regulatory history of Paraguayan manufacturers operating under the maquila regime to supply Brazil and the wider Mercosur market, for foreign principals managing reputational, contractual and customs risk.

matters.title: Asset tracing and judgment support
matters.text: Identifying real estate, vehicles, companies and business interests connected to Paraguayan debtors through registry and cadastral records, and coordinating with Paraguayan counsel on precautionary measures and recognition of foreign judgments or arbitral awards.

matters.title: AML and integrity reviews
matters.text: Assessing whether counterparties, acquisition targets or intermediaries have links to money laundering, cigarette smuggling or public corruption matters reported in Paraguayan proceedings and media, for banks, investors and multinationals with Southern Cone exposure.

tdsc_approach: TDSC scopes Paraguay engagements from Nashville, beginning with a jurisdictional review of what the Civil Code registries, cadastral records and court files can lawfully show, and how Ley 7593/2025 and its phased implementation affect handling of personal data. We work from public registry extracts obtained through proper requests, published judgments, procurement and customs-related public data, media archives in Spanish and Portuguese, and records in Brazil, Argentina and the United States where structures cross borders. We do not claim access to the beneficial ownership registers or any restricted state database. Where interviews, site visits to farms or plants, or record retrieval are needed, we coordinate qualified Paraguayan professionals and counsel. Personal data is minimised, held securely and transferred only as needed for the engagement.

faqs.q: When does Paraguay's new data protection law apply?
faqs.a: Ley 7593/2025 was promulgated on 28 November 2025 and creates a national data protection agency under MITIC. Official statements in 2026 indicated it will take effect progressively from late 2027, with regulations setting concrete deadlines. Organisations handling Paraguayan personal data should prepare now, since investigations started today may still be underway when obligations bite.

faqs.q: Can I search Paraguay's beneficial ownership register?
faqs.a: Not as an open public database. Under Ley 6446/2019 legal persons file beneficial ownership details through the Abogacía del Tesoro, and SEPRELAD-supervised obliged entities must check registration. Private parties usually reconstruct ownership from registry filings, notarial deeds, court records and cross-border sources, or seek court-ordered disclosure through Paraguayan counsel.

faqs.q: Why does Ciudad del Este feature in so many due diligence reviews?
faqs.a: Its role as a re-export hub on the borders with Brazil and Argentina brings large volumes of electronics, tobacco and consumer goods trade, along with reported contraband, counterfeit and money laundering risk. Counterparties there often have thin public footprints, so ownership, litigation and reputational research typically combines Paraguayan and Brazilian sources.

faqs.q: Are private investigators licensed in Paraguay?
faqs.a: We have not identified a dedicated licensing regime for private investigators in Paraguay, so the legal position is confirmed with Paraguayan counsel for each matter. Interception and access to restricted state records are reserved to authorities. TDSC does not conduct field work itself in Paraguay and coordinates qualified local professionals where lawful inquiries on the ground are needed.

faqs.q: How is land ownership verified in Paraguay?
faqs.a: Through the real estate registry and the national cadastre, supported by notarial deeds and, where relevant, survey and environmental records. Overlapping titles and disputes over rural land are a known issue, so diligence on farmland usually includes checking title history, encumbrances, pending litigation and on-the-ground occupation through a local professional.
